subject: SIG: Subprocessor inventory and evidence request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@securecloud.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: Subprocessor breakdown & evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Tom / SecureCloud procurement team,

We're preparing a SIG submission as part of a routine customer audit and need a current subprocessor inventory and supporting evidence from SecureCloud. Can you provide the following by EOD Fri (13 Feb)?

- A full export (CSV preferred) of all subprocessors you engage that process or store customer data: cloud infra providers, monitoring/telemetry, error tracking, support/crm, backups, analytics, CDNs, identity providers. Include the vendor name, service role (e.g., metrics, auth), region(s), and whether they handle production PII.
- Copies or links to the latest SOC 2 / ISO / third-party attestations for those subprocessors (or confirmation of coverage under your contract).
- Signed DPA status or date of last DPA update for each subprocessor.
- Short notes on where logs and telemetry are retained and whether they contain customer content/PII.
- Any existing contract language around subprocessors that we can cite in the SIG (one paragraph max).

If you can also attach a completed SIG subprocessor CSV or your vendor inventory export, that would be ideal. We are happy to accept a preliminary export and follow up on gaps.

This is for a Redwood customer compliance request; I"ll loop priyom (security) and marissa (privacy/procurement) to validate. Let me know if the timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Partnerships (on behalf of Compliance)
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment requested: subprocessor-inventory-export (CSV)
From: Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@securecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@securecloud.com, procurement@securecloud.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Subprocessor breakdown & evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the heads-up — we can provide an export and the SOC2 link. I"ve attached a preliminary CSV export (see securecloud_subprocessor_inventory_20260211.csv) which lists our current subcontractors and their roles. A few notes:

- The CSV is best-effort and includes cloud infra, telemetry, support, and analytics vendors.
- Our SOC 2 Type II report covers core infra and identity providers; I"ll send a secure access link for the full report.
- For some of the smaller partners (local delivery/third-party integrations), we will need to confirm DPA status; we expect to have confirmations within 72 hours.

If you need the data in a different format for your SIG spreadsheet, say the Drive template you referenced, I can export that as well.

Tom
Head of Procurement
SecureCloud

---
Attachments: securecloud_subprocessor_inventory_20260211.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@securecloud.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Subprocessor breakdown & evidence for upcoming audit

Tom — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying asks before you finalize: 

- Please call out which telemetry/error-tracking vendors ingest full request/response payloads vs. only aggregated metrics. We need to flag any that might collect customer content.
- For support platforms (Zendesk, Intercom, etc.) list whether ticket attachments/logs are persisted and where.
- If any subprocessor is covered by your SOC2 via subservice organization carve-outs (i.e., covered indirectly), mark that explicitly in the CSV.

I"ve attached a link to our SIG template (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cSigSpreadsheet) — if you can drop the CSV into the "subprocessors" tab that will save us reconciliation time.

Marissa — can you take point on confirming whether the SOC2 link Tom sends is sufficient for our customer? Prio: validate coverage and datedness. Priyom — once we have the CSV I"ll hand off to you for technical review on PII/PII-in-telemetry.

Best,
Rishi

> On Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@securecloud.com> wrote:
> > Thanks for the heads-up — we can provide an export and the SOC2 link. I've attached a preliminary CSV export...
From: security@securecloud.com <security@securecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: tom.brewer@securecloud.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Subprocessor breakdown & evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Rishi / team,

Attached is an updated subprocessor inventory and our completed SIG answers focused on subprocessors (file: securecloud_sig_answers_20260215.pdf). Key highlights:

- Primary cloud provider: Google Cloud Platform (us-central1, us-east4) — handles compute, storage, backups. GCP is SOC 2 compliant (we provided link).
- Monitoring & metrics: Datadog (US region) — aggregates host/APP metrics, does not store full request/response payloads by default.
- Error tracking: Sentry (EU region for EU customers) — captures stack traces and error context. We flagged where customer-identifiable fields are redacted.
- Support/CRM: Zendesk — ticket bodies and attachments are retained for 365 days; attachments are stored in AWS S3 (US).
- Analytics: Mixpanel (US) — only anonymized event data sent for product analytics.

Attachments and links provided: the CSV export (securecloud_subprocessor_inventory_20260215.csv), the SIG-focused answers PDF (securecloud_sig_answers_20260215.pdf), and a small text file with a secure link to our SOC2 report (securecloud_soc2_access_link.txt).

Note on coverage: our SOC2 Type II report covers our control environment and subservice organizations referenced in the CSV. Where coverage is partial or subject-specific, we flagged it in the "coverage_notes" column of the CSV.

If you need vendor-level DPAs, we can provide redacted DPAs for specific vendors on request — internal legal needs approval for each redaction.

Regards,
SecureCloud Security Team

---
Attachments: securecloud_subprocessor_inventory_20260215.csv, securecloud_sig_answers_20260215.pdf, securecloud_soc2_access_link.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 14:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Subprocessor breakdown & evidence for upcoming audit

Folks — got SecureCloud"s updated CSV and SIG answers. Quick summary for our intake: 

- Files received: securecloud_subprocessor_inventory_20260215.csv, securecloud_sig_answers_20260215.pdf, and a secure link to their SOC2.
- Notable subprocessors called out: GCP (infra), Datadog (metrics), Sentry (error tracking), Zendesk (support), Mixpanel (analytics). Regions called out in CSV; Sentry set to EU for EU customers.
- They flagged several smaller partners where DPA confirmations are pending — Tom said that should be closed within ~72 hours.

Action items: 
- Marissa: please review the SOC2 link and the SIG answers PDF for coverage gaps (is the SOC2 dated within 12 months and does it explicitly cover the infra and identity providers?). Mark any vendor that requires a redacted DPA and request it from Tom.
- Priyom: run a quick PII-in-telemetry check on Datadog & Sentry entries in the CSV. Flag any entries that indicate full request/response retention.
- I'll follow up with Tom if we need redacted DPAs or an attest letter for smaller partners.

I'll log this on the HubSpot ticket (HS-23456) and drop the CSV into our SIG spreadsheet at the Drive link. If you need me to escalate to legal for DPA redactions, say the word.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
